The 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, awarded in particular to the creators of AlphaFold, established AI as a tool of biology. Two years on, the announcements are multiplying: protein binders with “ten times the affinity”, agents proposing drugs against AMD or leukaemia, the first phase 3 trial of a molecule designed by generative AI. Yet in medicine, the distance between a hypothesis and a treatment is measured in years and in thousands of patients. As of the date of this article, no drug discovered by AI has been authorised by a regulatory agency, according to the sources consulted. This article puts every result back in its place on the scale of evidence.
L&#39;IA accélère-t-elle réellement la m: Is AI really speeding up the development of drugs, or only the upstream stages, the least costly and the least risky ones? And how can this acceleration be reconciled with two strong European constraints: the protection of health data and the prevention of biological dual use?

Les modèles de structure : AlphaFold 3 p: Structure models: AlphaFold 3 predicts the shape of complexes between proteins, nucleic acids and small molecules; its open competitors are OpenFold3 and Boltz-2 (article 1).
Les modèles de séquences : Evo 2 pour le: Sequence models: Evo 2 for genomes, ESM3 for proteins. ESM3, published in Science in 2025, was used to design a fluorescent protein far removed from known natural proteins (doi 10.1126/science.ads0018).
Les agents de raisonnement : Co-Scientis: Reasoning agents: Co-Scientist, Robin, Mythos, which combine literature, databases and tools (article 2).
AlphaFold : la référence, avec ses limit: AlphaFold: the benchmark, and its limits
L&#39;Académie royale des sciences de Su: In 2024 the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences honoured Demis Hassabis and John Jumper for protein structure prediction, and David Baker for the computational design of proteins (Nobel Prize). AlphaFold 3, published in Nature on 8 May 2024, extends prediction to complexes with ligands and nucleic acids. The authors list a number of limitations: chirality violations, “hallucinations” of ordered structures in disordered regions, prediction of static structures rather than dynamic ensembles. Most of the authors declare commercial interests. Code and weights were made available for academic research in November 2024 (Google).
L&#39;essai de phase 2a publié dans <a h: The phase 2a trial published in Nature Medicine concerns rentosertib, from Insilico Medicine, a TNIK kinase inhibitor against idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, whose target and molecule were reportedly identified by AI. Method: randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 71 patients in 21 centres in China, 12 weeks. Primary endpoint: safety (the proportion of patients with at least one adverse event), not efficacy. Exploratory result: forced vital capacity improved by 98.4 ml in the 60 mg group, against a fall of 20.3 ml on placebo. 16 of the 71 patients stopped treatment, more of them in the high-dose groups; some discontinuations are linked to liver injury. Employees of the sponsor took part in the design, the analysis and the interpretation.
Le 10 septembre 2026, Insilico a annoncé: On 10 September 2026, Insilico announced the first patient dosed in the phase 3 GENESIS-IPF-3 trial: 320 participants planned in 47 centres in China, 52 weeks, with the annual decline in forced vital capacity as the primary endpoint (Insilico Medicine). The coordinator estimates that it will take three to four years “under favourable conditions” to reach an authorisation. The molecule is not authorised anywhere.
Demis Hassabis a déclaré en janvier 2026: Demis Hassabis said in January 2026 at Davos that Alphabet’s subsidiary Isomorphic Labs “plans to have its first clinical trials by the end of 2026”, whereas a year earlier he had been targeting the end of 2025 (Reuters). The company’s public announcements up to 7 October 2026 make no mention of a patient dosed (Isomorphic Labs): information not confirmed to date.
Co-Scientist (Google) : binimetinib acti: Co-Scientist (Google): binimetinib active at nanomolar concentrations on acute myeloid leukaemia cell lines; vorinostat active on fibrotic liver organoids (Nature). Level IV and PC.
Robin (FutureHouse) : ripasudil, déjà pr: Robin (FutureHouse): ripasudil, already prescribed for glaucoma, increases phagocytosis in cultured retinal epithelial cells, a lead for dry AMD (FutureHouse). Level IV.
Le repositionnement de médicaments déjà: Repurposing drugs that are already authorised reduces the toxicological risk, but not the need for efficacy trials.
Les revendications des modèles frontier: The claims made for the frontier models
Liants protéiques dix fois plus affins q: Protein binders with ten times the affinity of the best designs from the Adaptyv Bio competitions on three targets (EGFR, Nipah G, 15-PGDH); a competing design aimed at another region of Nipah G reaches comparable affinity (about 1.4 nM)
BI, validé par deux organisations extern: BI, validated by two unnamed external organisations
Taux de réussite de près de 50 % sur 12: Success rate of nearly 50% on 12 targets, compared with 10 to 15% usually
Hypothèses de biologie moléculaire préfé: Molecular biology hypotheses preferred in about 80% of blind comparisons by the company’s scientists

Une forte affinité de liaison mesurée in: A high binding affinity measured in vitro is a first step. It says nothing about specificity, stability, immunogenicity or therapeutic efficacy.
Evo 2, publié dans Nature en 2026, a été: Evo 2, published in Nature in 2026, was trained on genomes from every domain of life. Of 285 bacteriophage genomes designed, 16 propagated and inhibited their target bacterium (Arc Institute). This is a remarkable proof of concept and a modest success rate, which illustrates the gap between generation and function.
La prédiction de structure par IA est un: AI structure prediction is an established scientific achievement (P, Nobel 2024).
Des agents produisent des hypothèses de: Agents produce repurposing hypotheses that pass in vitro and organoid tests (P + IV / PC).
Une molécule issue d&#39;une plateforme: A molecule from an AI platform has shown acceptable tolerability and an exploratory signal of efficacy in phase 2a (CL, small sample, sponsor involved).
Selon une analyse de BCG portant sur les: According to a BCG analysis of the pipelines of “AI-native” companies, molecules discovered by AI pass phase 1 in 80 to 90% of cases, but phase 2 in about 40% of cases, a rate close to historical averages, on a small sample (Drug Discovery Today, 2024).
Lecture : l&#39;IA semble produire des m: Reading: AI appears to produce molecules with the right pharmacological properties; nothing yet proves that it is better at choosing the targets that work in patients.
L&#39;effet réel sur la durée totale de: The real effect on total development time: Insilico claims 18 months up to candidate nomination, but most of the time is spent in the clinic.
La généralisation des benchmarks de conc: How far protein design benchmarks generalise beyond the chosen targets.
Les biais des données : la littérature b: Data bias: the biomedical literature over-represents positive results, and Co-Scientist acknowledges that it has no access to negative results.
La frontière entre usage thérapeutique e: The boundary between therapeutic use and malicious use (see below).
Anthropic a évalué la capacité de Mythos: Anthropic has evaluated Mythos 5’s ability to predict properties of adeno-associated virus capsids, the vectors used in gene therapy, noting that the same ability could help design dangerous viruses (Anthropic). This is why Fable blocks professional biology queries, and Mythos is open only to vetted professionals in the United States. Microsoft and its partners showed that open tools could reformulate toxins so as to get past DNA suppliers’ filters, then improved those filters (C&EN). Gigi Kwik Gronvall (Johns Hopkins) warns: “one day there will be a problem that cannot be solved by better screening or better technology”.

Deux points d&#39;architecture comptent: Two architectural points matter for Europe. First, federated learning: Eli Lilly’s TuneLab programme gives biotechs access to models trained on about $1 billion worth of proprietary data, without each participant’s data leaving its own environment (NVIDIA). Second, the hosting of health data, discussed below.
Les données de santé françaises sont un: French health data is a rare asset: the Système national des données de santé (SNDS) covers almost the whole population. Its use by researchers has been held back by the hosting of the Health Data Hub at Microsoft: because of US extraterritorial laws (Cloud Act, FISA), the CNIL has never authorised the transfer of the SNDS to the Hub. On 23 April 2026, the government chose Scaleway to host it; a copy of the SNDS could be transferred between late 2026 and early 2027 (Le Monde).
Au niveau européen, le règlement sur l&#: At European level, the regulation on the European Health Data Space (EHDS, Regulation 2025/327) entered into force on 26 March 2025 and progressively organises the secondary use of health data for research (European Commission). On the AI side, the AI Act rules for high-risk systems embedded in regulated products, such as medical devices, have been postponed to 2 August 2028 by the digital omnibus (European Parliament).
L&#39;Inserm affiche l&#39;IA comme levi: Inserm presents AI as a lever for exploiting health data (Inserm), but we have found no documented public programme combining frontier agents and SNDS data (information not confirmed).
Le Royaume-Uni a choisi une mission chif: The United Kingdom has chosen a quantified mission: “trial-ready” drugs in 100 days by 2030, with £8 million for the OpenBind consortium at the Diamond synchrotron, tasked with producing protein–ligand structure data (techUK). It is a target, not a result, but it illustrates a strategy: investing in high-quality experimental data rather than in the model.
Enfin, l&#39;asymétrie d&#39;accès pèse: Finally, the asymmetry of access weighs on European research: Anthropic’s best-performing model for protein design is not accessible outside the United States to date.

L&#39;IA a déjà transformé la biologie s: AI has already transformed structural biology and is beginning to speed up the generation of hypotheses and the design of molecules. It has not yet demonstrated that it increases the probability that a drug works in patients. The coming years will be decisive: the results of rentosertib’s phase 3, Isomorphic’s first trials, and above all the phase 2 success rate of molecules derived from AI. For France, the challenge is to open its health data to research within a sovereign framework, at the very moment when the best biology models are reserved for US users.
